title: The Alibi Photograph
description: Clearing out your late father's attic, you find a dated photograph from a murder scene twenty years ago — and in the crowd behind the police tape, unmistakably, stands you.

n1.caption: In your father's dusty attic you find a yellowed photograph: police tape, a crowd, a murder scene dated twenty years ago — and there in the crowd, wearing the jacket you own, is you.

n2a.caption: The photographer's studio is still open, the darkroom light burning red. On the drying line hang hundreds of prints from different decades — and your face is in every single one.

n2b.caption: The detective studies the photo, then looks up at you slowly. She opens a drawer and slides an identical print across the desk: 'It's evidence in an open case. We've been waiting for you.'

n3a.caption: The photographer turns from the enlarger. The face is older, lined — but unmistakably yours. 'You're right on schedule,' they say, reaching for a camera.

n3b.caption: You burn every print in a trash can and drive home shaking — but your mailbox holds a fresh envelope. Inside: the same photograph, and the date stamped on the back is tomorrow.

n3c.caption: 'The murder in that photo was never solved — until someone walked in twenty years later and solved it.' She taps the file. 'The case file says the detective was you.'

n3d.caption: You sprint for your car — but in the rearview mirror, lit by the studio window, you see someone inside already feeding photos into a fire. It's you, and they're smiling.
